entities.name: Waddy Thompson, Jr.
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Waddy Thompson Jr. (1798–1868) was a South Carolina Whig congressman and United States Minister to Mexico (1842–44) during the tense years before the Mexican–American War. A lawyer-politician from the upcountry, he served in the House where he mixed states’-rights Southern politics with nationalist Whig instincts on commerce and diplomacy.

As minister in Mexico City he managed claims, release of prisoners, and communication in a climate of Texas annexation controversy and mutual suspicion. His published Recollections of Mexico offered American readers a Whig-inflected portrait of Mexican society and politics on the eve of war.

Thompson’s mission is a window onto antebellum diplomacy that failed to prevent the slide toward 1846.
